content.text:
All three changes are in and the 45 unit tests pass, but nothing has run in the sandbox yet. Speed and quality are unproven until a test run.

**1. Shorter prompts** (cuts input tokens on every browser step)
- Navigating agents no longer get browser-use's built-in system prompt of about 23k characters (about 5k tokens). A short version of about 1.7k characters replaces it, with the same reply format and rules.
- I removed browser-use actions our agents never need: web search, its model-based page extraction, screenshots/PDF, uploads and its scratch file system. They no longer appear in every prompt, and the model can't waste steps on them. Web search would also try to reach hosts we aren't allowed to contact.
- I rewrote goals, hints, rules, tool descriptions and analyst instructions in short "caveman" style. All rules, traps and German terms are kept, and the JSON shapes the analysts must fill are unchanged.

**2. Parallel tabs**
- **Tab handling** (`swarm/browser_agent.py`): each `browse()` runs in its own tab, either the browser's main tab or a new one. Tabs in the same browser share login cookies, so one login covers them all. Each agent sees only its own tab plus popups, never another agent's tab. Each new tab opens in its own window, because Chrome slows down timers in background tabs.
- **Tab lifetime:** a tab closes as soon as its job ends. ERP tabs take the next item from a shared queue and close when it is empty.
- **ERP:** while waiting for requirements, the main tab logs in and passes the access gate. Then up to 5 workers on browser 2 handle the catalogue groups at the same time. Before, one worker per browser did them one after another. The `ErpHelper` classes are removed.
- **Mail:** the main tab logs in while the brief is being read. Then all topic groups are searched at once: discount approvals; condition rules plus technical release; the remaining topics two per tab, up to 3 extra tabs. `done.mail_core` and `done.mail` are still set as before.
- **Tender:** a short first pass logs in, reads the overview and registers interest. Then the documents (main tab) and the Q&A (second tab) are read at the same time.
- **Spec:** stays one tab, because each step depends on the previous one.

**3. Flash mode**
- Navigating and extracting agents now reply with a short memory plus actions only, without the separate thinking and evaluation fields. Replies are capped at 2,000 tokens, which stops the runaway replies we saw (one took 101 s).
- The bid submitter keeps full reasoning and browser-use's full prompt (`flash=False`).
- Analysts never used the model's separate reasoning pass, so they are unchanged.

**Checks:** I tested the tab handling against a local headless Chromium. Each session focused only its own tab and saw only that tab, and a closed tab reopened correctly. I also added unit tests for this, for the removed actions, and for the short prompt. `docs/SWARM.md` is updated.

**Risks to watch in the next test run:**
- About 13 browser agents now call the model at once, close to half of the 32-call limit before analyst calls are added.
- All agents run in one Python process, and browser-use processes every page on that single core.
- Without the thinking fields, the model might make more navigation mistakes. If quality drops on one site, that scraper can switch back with `flash=False`.

Nothing is committed yet. Should I commit and start a test run (`atira test-run . --follow`) once the current run finishes, then compare the two with `compare_runs`?

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_inputs
entries.description: What the agent system did in the browsers, as the platform recorded it: clicks and taps with x,y on the 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included), drags, scrolls and typing, each with its time on the run's clock, in time order. Typed text shows, with keys and tokens masked. Pair a time with run_screenshot to see the screen then.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

after.description: Continue after a previous page: its `next` value

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_screenshot
entries.description: A browser's screen at a time in the run, cut from its recording, with the clicks just before it marked (red: the latest) and the log lines around it. browser "all" puts every browser in one 2×2 image; frames {from, to, every} makes a filmstrip of up to 9 frames in one image. While a run is still going there is no recording yet: it shows the latest live frame. About 1.5k tokens an image.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

at.description: When, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works. Not needed with frames.

browser.description: Which browser, 1–4 (default 1), or "all" for every browser at once

frames.description: A filmstrip instead of one frame: {from, to, every}, times on the run's clock (every: e.g. 10s)

marks.description: Mark the clicks recorded just before (default true)

content.content: Give at (a time on the run's clock), or frames.

832

835	
836			Args:

		"""Enable lifecycle events and network monitoring for a page target.

		This is called once per page when it's created, avoiding handler accumulation.
		Registers a SINGLE lifecycle handler per session that stores events for navigations to consume.

		Args:
			cdp_session: The CDP session to enable monitoring on
		"""
		try:
			# Enable Page domain first (required for lifecycle events)
			await cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Page.enable(session_id=cdp_session.session_id)

			# Enable lifecycle events (load, DOMContentLoaded, networkIdle, etc.)
			await cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Page.setLifecycleEventsEnabled(
				params={'enabled': True}, session_id=cdp_session.session_id
			)

			# Enable network monitoring for networkIdle detection
			await cdp_session.cdp_client.send.Network.enable(session_id=cdp_session.session_id)

			# Initialize lifecycle event storage for this session (thread-safe)
			from collections import deque

			cdp_session._lifecycle_events = deque(maxlen=50)  # Keep last 50 events
			cdp_session._lifecycle_lock = asyncio.Lock()

			# Register ONE handler per session that stores events
			def on_lifecycle_event(event, session_id=None):
				event_name = event.get('name', 'unknown')
				event_loader_id = event.get('loaderId', 'none')

				# Find which target this session belongs to
				target_id_from_event = None
				if session_id:
					target_id_from_event = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id)

				# Check if this event is for our target
				if target_id_from_event == cdp_session.target_id:
					# Store event for navigations to consume
					event_data = {
						'name': event_name,
						'loaderId': event_loader_id,
						'timestamp': asyncio.get_event_loop().time(),
					}
					# Append is atomic in CPython
					try:
						cdp_session._lifecycle_events.append(event_data)
					except Exception as e:
						# Only log errors, not every event
						self.logger.error(f'[SessionManager] Failed to store lifecycle event: {e}')

			# Register the handler ONCE (this is the only place we register)
			cdp_session.cdp_client.register.Page.lifecycleEvent(on_lifecycle_event)

		except Exception as e:
			# Don't fail - target might be short-lived or already detached

async def _with_cdp(browser: int, call):
    client = CDPClient(await _browser_ws(browsers.cdp_urls()[browser % len(browsers.cdp_urls())]))
    await client.start()

class Tab:
    """One tab of browser `browser`, owned by one agent (one browse() at a time). `Tab(b)` is a new tab, opened at the
    first browse(); `main_tab(b)` is the tab the browser started with. Locally (no CDP) every browse() starts its own
    Chromium, so a Tab is only a label there."""

    def __init__(self, browser: int, main: bool = False):
        self.browser, self.main = browser, main
        self.target_id: str | None = None

    def claim(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        self.target_id = target_id
        _OWNERS[target_id] = self

    async def open(self) -> None:
        """Create the tab now (before the session connects) so no other agent ever sees it unowned."""
        if self.target_id or self.main or not browsers.cdp_urls():
            return
        # A window of its own: the tab stays the visible one there, so Chrome does not throttle its timers the way it
        # throttles background tabs (pages that load or retry with timers would crawl).
        made = await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.createTarget(
            params={"url": "about:blank", "newWindow": True}))
        self.claim(made["targetId"])

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the tab (never the browser's main tab)."""
        target, self.target_id = self.target_id, None
        if not target or self.main:
            return
        _OWNERS.pop(target, None)
        try:
            await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.closeTarget(params={"targetId": target}))
        except Exception as error:      # already closed / browser gone
            log.debug("closing tab failed: %s", error)


def main_tab(browser: int) -> Tab:
    return _MAIN_TABS.setdefault(browser, Tab(browser, main=True))


_all_page_targets = SessionManager.get_all_page_targets


def _visible_page_targets(self) -> list:
    """What a session sees as "the browser's tabs": its own tab first, then tabs nobody owns (popups); never the tabs
    of other agents. browser-use derives its tab list, focus and new-tab reuse from this."""
    targets = _all_page_targets(self)
    tab = getattr(self.browser_session, "_tab", None)
    if tab is None:
        return targets
    return ([t for t in targets if t.target_id == tab.target_id]
            + [t for t in targets if t.target_id != tab.target_id and t.target_id not in _OWNERS])


SessionManager.get_all_page_targets = _visible_page_targets


class RobustSession(BrowserSession):
    """A BrowserSession whose navigation recovers from a tab stuck while loading: stop the old load and retry once.
    It works in its own `Tab` (set `_tab` before starting)."""

    _tab: Any = PrivateAttr(default=None)

    async def connect(self, cdp_url: str | None = None):
        await super().connect(cdp_url)
        tab, focus = self._tab, self.agent_focus_target_id
        if tab is not None and focus and tab.target_id != focus:
            alive = {t.target_id for t in _all_page_targets(self.session_manager)}
            if tab.target_id not in alive:      # a main tab's first use, or the agent closed its tab: adopt this one
                _OWNERS.pop(tab.target_id or "", None)
                tab.claim(focus)
        return self

    async def _navigate_and_wait(self, url, target_id, timeout=None, wait_until="load"):
        try:
            return await super()._navigate_and_wait(url, target_id, timeout=timeout, wait_until=wait_until)
        except RuntimeError as error:
            if "timed out" not in str(error):
                raise
            log.warning("navigation stuck, stopping the old load and retrying: %s", url)
            session = await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=False)
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(session.cdp_client.send.Page.stopLoading(session_id=session.session_id), 5)
            except Exception as stop_error:
                log.debug("stopLoading failed: %s", stop_error)
            return await super()._navigate_and_wait(url, target_id, timeout=timeout, wait_until=wait_until)

async def _enable_page_monitoring_routed(self, cdp_session) -> None:
    """browser-use registers one lifecycle handler per page target, but the CDP client keeps only ONE handler per event
    (the last one), and that handler drops events of every other target. With several tabs in a browser, navigations
    in all but the last-attached tab then waited for load events that never came (3-8 s per navigation). Here one
    handler per client routes each event to the queue of its own target."""
    await _enable_page_monitoring(self, cdp_session)
    events = getattr(cdp_session, "_lifecycle_events", None)
    if events is None:
        return
    routes = self.__dict__.setdefault("_lifecycle_routes", {})
    routes[cdp_session.target_id] = events

    def route(event, session_id=None):
        target = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if session_id else None
        queue = routes.get(target)
        if queue is not None:
            queue.append({"name": event.get("name", "unknown"), "loaderId": event.get("loaderId", "none"),
                          "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()})

    cdp_session.cdp_client.register.Page.lifecycleEvent(route)

class RobustSession(BrowserSession):
    """A BrowserSession whose navigation recovers from a tab stuck while loading: stop the old load and retry once.
    It works in its own `Tab` (set `_tab` before starting), with focus emulation on: with several windows only one has
    the OS focus, and in the others typed text and focus-dependent page scripts did nothing (logins "did not register",
    links "did not navigate"). Playwright enables the same emulation on every page for this reason."""

    _tab: Any = PrivateAttr(default=None)
    _focus_emulated: set = PrivateAttr(default_factory=set)

    async def connect(self, cdp_url: str | None = None):
        await super().connect(cdp_url)
        tab, focus = self._tab, self.agent_focus_target_id
        if tab is not None and focus and tab.target_id != focus:
            alive = {t.target_id for t in _all_page_targets(self.session_manager)}
            if tab.target_id not in alive:      # a main tab's first use, or the agent closed its tab: adopt this one
                _OWNERS.pop(tab.target_id or "", None)
                tab.claim(focus)
        if tab is not None and focus:
            await self.get_or_create_cdp_session(focus, focus=True)     # turns focus emulation on for the tab
        return self

    async def get_or_create_cdp_session(self, target_id=None, focus: bool = True):
        session = await super().get_or_create_cdp_session(target_id, focus=focus)
        if focus and self._tab is not None and session.session_id not in self._focus_emulated:
            self._focus_emulated.add(session.session_id)
            try:
                await session.cdp_client.send.Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(
                    params={"enabled": True}, session_id=session.session_id)
            except Exception as error:
                log.debug("focus emulation failed: %s", error)
        return session

async def _enable_page_monitoring_routed(self, cdp_session) -> None:
    """browser-use registers one lifecycle handler per page target, but the CDP client keeps only ONE handler per event
    (the last one), and that handler drops events of every other target. With several tabs in a browser, navigations
    in all but the last-attached tab then waited for load events that never came (3-8 s per navigation). Here one
    handler per client routes each event to the queue of its own target."""
    await _enable_page_monitoring(self, cdp_session)
    events = getattr(cdp_session, "_lifecycle_events", None)
    if events is None:
        return
    routes = self.__dict__.setdefault("_lifecycle_routes", {})
    routes[cdp_session.target_id] = events

    def route(event, session_id=None):
        target = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if session_id else None
        queue = routes.get(target)
        if queue is not None:
            queue.append({"name": event.get("name", "unknown"), "loaderId": event.get("loaderId", "none"),
                          "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()})

    cdp_session.cdp_client.register.Page.lifecycleEvent(route)

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: scraper   SITE: webmail (role "mail")
"""Reads the mails that matter for this tender, saved as page evidence ("mail.page").

The main tab logs in while the brief is being read; then every topic group gets a tab of its own (sharing the login)
and all are searched at once:
- core (sets done.mail_core when both are finished): the sales director's discount approvals (main tab), and the
  condition-rule + technical-release mails;
- the other release mails the brief names (packaging, delivery, setup pools, project bonus, FX, price indices), two
  topics per tab (sets done.mail when all are finished).
The signing TAN is NOT read here: the submitter asks for it when it signs (agents/submit_bid.py)."""
import asyncio

from swarm import Phase, register  # noqa: F401
from swarm.scraper import SiteScraper
from swarm.sites import site_for

CORE_TOPICS = ("rabatt", "rabattfreigabe", "konditionsregeln", "technikfreigabe")
TOPICS_PER_TAB = 2
MAX_REST_TABS = 3

SEARCH_RULES = (
    "Mailbox search combines words with AND and shows limited hits: search exact tender reference plus ONE topic word "
    "at a time ('<reference> <topic>'). Search inbox AND archive folder (page through results). Look-alike references "
    "(same reference with suffix) and other tenders do not count; drafts, previews, superseded mails look similar: "
    "read each candidate message.\n"
    "Every message whose subject or text names this tender's reference and the topic: read_page it with topic "
    "'<topic> mail' - several selected messages at once with read_page(urls=[their links]) - (read_page also reads "
    "collapsed or locked parts, no need to unlock). Reading pane shows no message text -> open message's own page "
    "('open original'/message link) and read that. Skip signing-TAN mails.")


@register
class MailScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "mail"
    browser = 3
    max_steps = 26
    hints = ("Webmail habits: cookie wall after login; maintenance popups (close them, never follow their links); "
             "inbox and archive folder; paged result lists; message headers (sender, date) in collapsed "
             "'envelope/headers' section, which read_page includes.")

    async def login(self) -> None:
        """Log in once in the main tab, so the topic tabs start logged in (they would log in themselves otherwise)."""
        try:
            await self.browse("Log in, accept cookie wall, close popups, open inbox. Do NOT search yet. Then done.",
                              max_steps=8)
        except Exception as error:
            self.log.warning("login browse failed: %s", error)

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            facts, _ = await asyncio.gather(self.wait_brief(), self.login())
            facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or facts
            discount = (f"Find discount approvals for this tender (sender: "
                        f"{facts.get('director_sender') or 'the sales director'}). Topic words to try: "
                        f"{facts.get('discount_topic') or 'Rabatt'}, Rabattfreigabe.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            rules = ("Find condition-rule mails (Konditionsregeln) and technical release mails (Technikfreigabe) for "
                     f"this tender, if they exist, one search per topic.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            topics = [t for t in (facts.get("mail_topics") or []) if t and t.lower() not in CORE_TOPICS]
            groups = [topics[i:i + TOPICS_PER_TAB] for i in range(0, len(topics), TOPICS_PER_TAB)]
            if len(groups) > MAX_REST_TABS:            # keep the tab count bounded: spread the topics evenly
                groups = [topics[i::MAX_REST_TABS] for i in range(MAX_REST_TABS)]
            rest = [f"Find release mails for this tender on these topics, one search per topic: {', '.join(g)}.\n"
                    f"{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done." for g in groups]

            async def core() -> None:
                outs = await asyncio.gather(self.browse_until_done(discount, attempts=2),
                                            self.browse_in_tabs([rules], max_steps=26))
                await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", outs[0]["summary"])
                await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)

            await asyncio.gather(core(), self.browse_in_tabs(rest, max_steps=26) if rest else asyncio.sleep(0))
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail", True)

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: scraper   SITE: webmail (role "mail")
"""Reads the mails that matter for this tender, saved as page evidence ("mail.page").

The main tab logs in while the brief is being read; then every topic group gets a tab of its own (sharing the login)
and all are searched at once:
- core (sets done.mail_core when both are finished): the sales director's discount approvals (main tab), and the
  condition-rule + technical-release mails;
- the other release mails the brief names (packaging, delivery, setup pools, project bonus, FX, price indices), two
  topics per tab (sets done.mail when all are finished).
The signing TAN is NOT read here: the submitter asks for it when it signs (agents/submit_bid.py)."""
import asyncio

from swarm import Phase, register  # noqa: F401
from swarm.scraper import SiteScraper
from swarm.sites import site_for

CORE_TOPICS = ("rabatt", "rabattfreigabe", "konditionsregeln", "technikfreigabe")
TOPICS_PER_TAB = 2
MAX_REST_TABS = 3

SEARCH_RULES = (
    "Mailbox search combines words with AND and shows limited hits: search exact tender reference plus ONE topic word "
    "at a time ('<reference> <topic>'). Search inbox AND archive folder (page through results). Look-alike references "
    "(same reference with suffix) and other tenders do not count; drafts, previews, superseded mails look similar: "
    "read each candidate message.\n"
    "Every message whose subject or text names this tender's reference and the topic: read_page it with topic "
    "'<topic> mail' - several selected messages at once with read_page(urls=[their links]) - (read_page also reads "
    "collapsed or locked parts, no need to unlock). Reading pane shows no message text -> open message's own page "
    "('open original'/message link) and read that. Skip signing-TAN mails.")


@register
class MailScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "mail"
    browser = 3
    max_steps = 26
    hints = ("Webmail habits: cookie wall after login; maintenance popups (close them, never follow their links); "
             "search may sit behind slider/robot gate: pass it with ONE fill_form (slider = its maximum, robot "
             "checkbox = true), not with evaluate; inbox and archive folder; paged result lists; message headers "
             "(sender, date) in collapsed 'envelope/headers' section, which read_page includes.")

    async def login(self) -> None:
        """Log in once in the main tab, so the topic tabs start logged in (they would log in themselves otherwise)."""
        try:
            await self.browse("Log in, accept cookie wall, close popups, open inbox. Do NOT search yet. Then done.",
                              max_steps=8)
        except Exception as error:
            self.log.warning("login browse failed: %s", error)

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            facts, _ = await asyncio.gather(self.wait_brief(), self.login())
            facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or facts
            discount = (f"Find discount approvals for this tender (sender: "
                        f"{facts.get('director_sender') or 'the sales director'}). Topic words to try: "
                        f"{facts.get('discount_topic') or 'Rabatt'}, Rabattfreigabe.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            rules = ("Find condition-rule mails (Konditionsregeln) and technical release mails (Technikfreigabe) for "
                     f"this tender, if they exist, one search per topic.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            topics = [t for t in (facts.get("mail_topics") or []) if t and t.lower() not in CORE_TOPICS]
            groups = [topics[i:i + TOPICS_PER_TAB] for i in range(0, len(topics), TOPICS_PER_TAB)]
            if len(groups) > MAX_REST_TABS:            # keep the tab count bounded: spread the topics evenly
                groups = [topics[i::MAX_REST_TABS] for i in range(MAX_REST_TABS)]
            rest = [f"Find release mails for this tender on these topics, one search per topic: {', '.join(g)}.\n"
                    f"{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done." for g in groups]

            async def core() -> None:
                outs = await asyncio.gather(self.browse_until_done(discount, attempts=2),
                                            self.browse_in_tabs([rules], max_steps=26))
                await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", outs[0]["summary"])
                await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)

            await asyncio.gather(core(), self.browse_in_tabs(rest, max_steps=26) if rest else asyncio.sleep(0))
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail", True)

content.text:
The tabs are opening. Each new tab gets its own window, and the live view only shows the top window of each browser, so they look missing. The real problems were three bugs that broke agents in those extra windows, and I've fixed all three in the code. Unit tests pass, but nothing has been tested in the sandbox yet. The current run (`run_d1ee764b7577c7dc`) is still on the old code.

**What the logs show**
- The tabs do run. At about 5:30 there were 5 mail agents, 2 tender agents and 5 ERP agents working at once.
- Calls are much cheaper: about 2k input tokens per call instead of 6–18k, and a typical call took 5 s instead of 14 s.
- ERP shared the login correctly: the new tabs logged "already logged in" and went straight to work.

**Bug 1: agents in windows without focus could not type or click.**
- Only one window per browser has the operating-system focus. In the other windows, typing and scripts that depend on focus did nothing.
- The logs show it: "Login stuck 12 steps; typed values not registering", "Slider stuck at value=0", and the main tender tab saying "Clicking tender link never navigates".
- One mail tab ended with 0 records after 25 steps.
- **Fix:** every agent's tab now has Chrome's focus emulation switched on, so each page behaves as if it had focus. Playwright does the same on every page for this reason.

**Bug 2: every navigation in a new tab waited 3–8 s for nothing.**
- This is the "No lifecycle events" warning. Browser-use registers one page-load handler per tab, but the underlying connection keeps only the last one registered, and that one drops events from every other tab.
- With one tab per browser this never showed up; with several, all but one tab waited out the full timeout on each page load.
- **Fix:** one shared handler now passes each page-load event to the tab it belongs to.

**Bug 3: a tab's next job restarted from the site's start page.**
- When a tab got a second job, browser-use opened the site's start URL from the goal again. The main tender tab lost the tender page it was on, and an ERP tab moving to its next item would lose its place the same way.
- **Fix:** a tab that has already been used now continues from its current page.

**Smaller fixes**
- Mail tabs did not share the login (each new tab showed the login form), and the search sits behind a slider-and-checkbox gate. Agents looped trying to unlock it with injected JavaScript. The mail hints now say: try `fill_form` once, then press End on the slider or click its right end, and never loop on JavaScript.
- `fill_form` now also reaches form fields inside web components (open shadow roots), which the mail login and slider use. Setting a slider to "max" now sets its real maximum.

**One decision for you on visibility:** I can put new tabs in the same window instead, so they show in the tab strip of the live view. The catch is that Chrome slows timers in background tabs, which can slow pages that load or retry on a timer. With focus emulation now on, the remaining risk is mainly that timer slowdown. I'd keep separate windows; say if you'd rather see real tabs.

**Next step:** the current run will keep stalling on the mail tabs until it hits its time limit. Should I cancel it and start a new test run with these fixes?

# Swarm guide

One process, one asyncio loop, many agents. Agents share a **blackboard**; the **orchestrator** runs them in phases.
Each person owns **one file in `agents/`** (no merge conflicts); shared code is in `swarm/` (change it by PR, small).

```
COLLECT (dataflow: scrapers + analysts, synchronised by done flags)  ->  VERIFY  ->  COMPUTE (plain code)  ->  SUBMIT
 scrapers save pages the MODEL chose; analysts turn them into results                                        enter bid, sign TAN
```

## Data flow (who waits for what)

```
BriefReader ──> results["brief"] (reference, scenario date, bidder, authorised senders), results["sites"] (role -> siteId)
TenderScraper (b0) login + overview, then documents (main tab) || Q&A (2nd tab)
                   ──tender.page──> done.tender ──> QuantityAnalyzer ──> results["tender"], results["quantities"]
SpecScraper   (b1) ──spec.page───> done.spec ───> RequirementAnalyzer ──> results["spec"], results["requirements"]
                                                        (+ Q&A amendments) ──> results["requirements_final"]
ErpScraper    (b2) logs in while waiting for results["requirements"] -> queue of catalogue groups worked by up to
                   ERP_TABS tabs at once ──erp.page──> done.erp ──> MaterialMatcher ──> results["erp"], results["materials"]
MailScraper   (b3) logs in while the brief is read, then one tab per topic group at once: approvals || conditions +
                   technical ──> done.mail_core; other release mails (2 topics per tab) ──> done.mail
                   ──mail.page──> DiscountAnalyzer ──> results["discount"], results["mail"], results["mailbox"]
EvidenceVerifier ──> results["verification"];  BidCalculator ──> results["bid"], results["answer"]
BidSubmitter (b0 main tab, full reasoning; TAN via a short browse on b3's main tab) ──> results["submission"]
```

Every scraper sets its `done.<role>` flag in a `finally`, so analysts never wait forever; every wait has a timeout
bounded by `ctx.time_left()`. Missing inputs degrade the bid (omitted positions, blank breakdown fields), never crash it.

## Files

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `swarm/blackboard.py` | `Evidence(kind, site, data, source, author, note)`, `Blackboard` (post/query/set/get/wait_for/dump/load) |
| `swarm/agent.py` | `Agent` base, `Phase`, `@register` |
| `swarm/context.py` | `ctx`: `task`, `board`, `llm`, `pool`, `site(id)`, `brief`, `time_left()`, `seconds_left()`, `lock(name)`, `shared` |
| `swarm/llm.py` | `ctx.llm.chat / ask / ask_json` (Qwen, concurrency-limited, usage counted), `parse_json` |
| `swarm/browser_agent.py` | `browse(ctx, goal, browser=n, tab=..., flash=...)`: **browser-use** on our CDP browser + Qwen, with our actions `read_page`, `record`, `fill_form`; `Tab` |
| `swarm/page_text.py` | the page extractor behind `read_page` (iframes, collapsed sections, tooltips, canvas labels, zero-width chars) |
| `swarm/forms.py` | the form filler behind `fill_form` (cascading selects via an apply button) |
| `swarm/extract.py` | analyst helpers: saved pages -> model extraction with a JSON shape (chunked, merged) |
| `swarm/normalize.py` | numbers (de-DE/en-US), dates (MM/DD vs DD/MM, ISO), references, German display format, cent rounding |
| `swarm/sites.py` | role -> siteId mapping (site names differ per dataset) |
| `swarm/scraper.py` | `SiteScraper`: set `role`, `browser`, write `goal()`; `self.browse(job)` for extra passes, `self.browse_in_tabs(jobs)` for parallel ones |
| `swarm/orchestrator.py` | discovery of `agents/*`, phases, timeouts, failure isolation, board dumps |
| `agents/*.py` | the agents. Header comment of each file: OWNER / ROLE / NEEDS / WRITES and the result shapes |

## How the model browses

The model (Qwen via browser-use) decides where to go. Three actions of ours make it fast and exact:

- `read_page(url?, topic?, next_page_link?)`: full text of the page it chose (hidden-but-real content included,
  decoys hidden from people excluded); with `next_page_link` it reads every page of a paged list; with `topic` the
  text is saved as Evidence `"<role>.page"` for the analysts. This is "extract a selected page / paginate a
  model-selected result set" from the rules: the model selects, the helper extracts.
- `record(kind, data, source, note)`: one fact.
- `fill_form(fields, apply_button?, then_click?)`: many fields of a form in one step (bid configurator).

Analysts then ask the model to extract a JSON shape from the saved text (`swarm/extract.py`) and apply the brief's
rules in code (latest dated record wins, withdrawn answers ignored, exact reference, authorised sender, ...).

## Contracts (agree before changing)

Evidence kinds: `<role>.page` (data: topic, url, title, pages, text) for saved pages; `record` kinds as the scraper's
goal names them (e.g. `mail.tan`). Results keys and shapes are documented at the top of each agent file.
Done flags: `done.tender`, `done.spec`, `done.erp`, `done.mail_core`, `done.mail`, `requirements_final`, `mail_final`.

## Local development

```powershell
atira models proxy                                   # terminal 1
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression   # terminal 2
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # whole swarm; dumps .swarm/board.json after each phase
$env:SWARM_DEADLINE_S="1200"                         # optional: simulate the 20-minute clock locally
$env:SWARM_ONLY="MaterialMatcher,BidCalculator"; $env:SWARM_BOARD_IN=".swarm/board.json"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # only these agents, on a saved board (no re-scraping)
uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```
`SWARM_BOARD_IN` is ignored in scored runs. `.swarm/` holds scouting data: git-ignored, never ship it.
Replaying analysts on a saved board: the done flags are in the board, so waits return immediately.

## Time budget (20-minute run)

`SUBMIT_RESERVE_S` (default 540 s, env `SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S`): collecting/analysing stops that long before expiry,
then VERIFY/COMPUTE (instant) and SUBMIT, which stops `FINAL_MARGIN_S` (40 s) before expiry.

## Fair-play rules for everyone (a reviewer reads the package)

- No scenario values anywhere (prices, material numbers, refs, logins, TANs, totals, dates, keys, transaction codes):
  not in prompts, hints, defaults, tests or notes. Tests use invented dummy data. Strategy is fine, values are not.
- The model decides where to go and what matters. Code may parse, page through model-selected results, validate,
  compute, fill forms. No fixed click paths, URL lists, or crawl-everything-then-one-prompt helpers.
- Only the provided CDP browsers; no extra Chromium; no hosts besides the platform and the 4 sites; models via the proxy.
- Do not write comments addressed to the reviewer.

## Robustness settings (learned from the first sandbox runs)

- No screenshots per step (`TextSession`): in the sandbox they stalled every step for 30 s. `read_page` covers canvas text.
- No browser-use loading animation: it loads a logo from an external host the sandbox cannot reach, which left the tab
  "loading" and every navigation in that browser timing out. `RobustSession` also stops a stuck load and retries once.
- Qwen's separate reasoning pass is off and replies are forced to a JSON object (`QwenChat`, `LLM.ask_json`): steps
  went from 10-75 s to a few seconds and the "invalid JSON / prose reply" failures stop.
- Scrapers, ERP items and the submitter retry an agent that stopped early, telling it what is already saved.
- Requirements are published early (as soon as a requirement table page is saved) so the ERP work starts sooner.

## Speed (each browsing step is one model call of ~14 s, most of it queue wait: fewer sequential steps = faster)

- Parallel tabs: the 4-browser limit does not limit tabs. Independent jobs run in tabs of their own (`Tab`,
  `browse_in_tabs`); tabs of one browser share its login cookies, so one login serves all. Each new tab gets its own
  window (no background-tab timer throttling) and is closed when its job ends. An agent sees only its own tab and
  unowned ones (popups), never another agent's tab. Rule: one browse() per tab at a time.
- Flash mode for navigating/extracting agents (default): replies are memory + actions only, with a compact system
  prompt (~0.6k instead of ~5k tokens) and a 2000-token reply cap. The bid submitter keeps full reasoning (`flash=False`).
- Unused browser-use actions (web search, LLM extract, screenshots, file system, uploads) are excluded: smaller schema
  in every prompt, and no wasted steps on them.
- Prompt text (goals, hints, rules, tool descriptions) is written tersely: every word is resent on every step.

## Work split (3 people) and how to iterate on your part

| Person | Agents | Iterate with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: tender + spec | `scrape_tender`, `scrape_spec`, `analyze_quantities`, `analyze_requirements` | `SWARM_ONLY=TenderScraper,QuantityAnalyzer` live; analysts on a saved board |
| B: ERP | `scrape_erp` (ErpScraper + its tab workers), `analyze_materials` | `SWARM_ONLY=ErpScraper,MaterialMatcher` on a board that has `requirements` |
| C: mail + shared | `scrape_mail`, `analyze_discount`, `compute_bid`, `submit_bid`, `swarm/*` | analysts/calculator on a saved board; `tests/test_rules.py` |

Loop: run your scraper live once -> it dumps `.swarm/board.json` -> replay your analyst on it as often as needed
(`SWARM_BOARD_IN`) -> check the result keys -> tune the goal/hints (strategy only) or the extraction shape -> repeat.
Then a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) to check timing; debug with `atira logs <run>`.

## Open items

- Tune goals/hints per site from test-run logs (`atira` MCP: `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_screenshot`).
- Submitter: watch the first real runs closely (wizard order, TAN timing).
- Cost: browser-use sends the goal every step; keep goals short.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Start a sandbox test run of this package (public data, unscored) and optionally follow its key log lines.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1                 # unit tests, then start the run; prints its id and page
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow         # ... and stream milestones + failures until the run ends
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Follow

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow
#>
param(
    [switch]$Follow,       # stream milestone/failure lines of the run's log until it ends
    [switch]$SkipTests,    # skip the local unit tests before packing
    [switch]$Open          # open the run page in the browser
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)

# Lines worth seeing while a run goes: phases, scraper/analyst results, the submission, and every kind of failure.
$Milestones = 'browse done|swarm phase|site roles|brief facts|early requirements|current revision|positions,|' +
              'discount \{|materials:|verification:|submission attempt|answer \(entered|model calls:|nothing saved|' +
              'tab job failed|timed out|failed|Traceback|FATAL|CRITICAL|No lifecycle events'

if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Write-Host "== unit tests"
    uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "unit tests failed: not starting a test run" }
}

Write-Host "== starting test run"
$openFlag = if ($Open) { @() } else { @("--no-open") }
$out = (& atira test-run . @openFlag | Out-String)
Write-Host $out.Trim()
$runId = [regex]::Match($out, 'run_[0-9a-f]{16}').Value
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

Write-Host "== run $runId  https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/$runId"
if (-not $Follow) {
    Write-Host "follow later: .\scripts\test-run.ps1 is done; use: atira logs $runId --follow"
    exit 0
}

# cmd merges stderr into stdout without PowerShell 5.1 wrapping each stderr line as an error record.
cmd /c "atira logs $runId --follow 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match $Milestones) { $_ } }
Write-Host "== log stream of $runId ended"

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Start a sandbox test run of this package (public data, unscored) and optionally follow its key log lines.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1                 # unit tests, then start the run; prints its id and page
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow         # ... and stream milestones + failures until the run ends
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Follow

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow
#>
param(
    [switch]$Follow,       # stream milestone/failure lines of the run's log until it ends
    [switch]$SkipTests,    # skip the local unit tests before packing
    [switch]$Open,         # open the run page in the browser
    [switch]$DryRun        # only show what would be packed
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)

# Lines worth seeing while a run goes: phases, scraper/analyst results, the submission, and every kind of failure.
$Milestones = 'browse done|swarm phase|site roles|brief facts|early requirements|current revision|positions,|' +
              'discount \{|materials:|verification:|submission attempt|answer \(entered|model calls:|nothing saved|' +
              'tab job failed|timed out|failed|Traceback|FATAL|CRITICAL|No lifecycle events'

if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Write-Host "== unit tests"
    uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "unit tests failed: not starting a test run" }
}

if ($DryRun) {
    atira test-run . --dry-run
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

Write-Host "== starting test run"
$openFlag = if ($Open) { @() } else { @("--no-open") }
$out = (& atira test-run . @openFlag | Out-String)
Write-Host $out.Trim()
$runId = [regex]::Match($out, 'run_[0-9a-f]{16}').Value
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

Write-Host "== run $runId  https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/$runId"
if (-not $Follow) {
    Write-Host "follow its log: atira logs $runId --follow"
    exit 0
}

# cmd merges stderr into stdout without PowerShell 5.1 wrapping each stderr line as an error record.
cmd /c "atira logs $runId --follow 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match $Milestones) { $_ } }
Write-Host "== log stream of $runId ended"

content.text:
Yes, tabs can sit side by side, and that's now the default. Each new agent tab opens in the browser's existing window, so the live view's tab strip shows every agent. Setting `TAB_WINDOWS=1` switches back to one window per tab.

The catch is that Chrome slows timers in background tabs. The focus emulation I added earlier keeps typing and logins working there. The open question is whether clicks reach background tabs reliably, because browser-use was built to click in the active tab. Only a test run will show that. If clicks fail, `TAB_WINDOWS=1` is the fallback.

The test-run script is `scripts/test-run.ps1`. It follows what I did before:
1. Runs the unit tests and stops if they fail.
2. Starts the run with `atira test-run . --no-open` and prints the run id and page.
3. With `-Follow`, streams only the key log lines: phase changes, results, the submission, failures, timeouts, tracebacks and the page-load warning.

```powershell
.\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow            # tests, start, follow key lines
.\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Open   # start right away, open the run page
.\scripts\test-run.ps1 -DryRun            # only list what would be uploaded
```
From Git Bash or a monitor: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow`

I checked it with `-DryRun`: the 45 unit tests pass and it would upload 45 files (311 KB). The script is included in the package because the upload only skips git-ignored files. It contains no scenario data.

Run `run_d1ee764b7577c7dc` is still going on the old code, which has the three tab bugs I fixed earlier. Should I cancel it and start a new run with `.\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow` under a monitor?

toolUseResult.originalFile:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Start a sandbox test run of this package (public data, unscored) and optionally follow its key log lines.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1                 # unit tests, then start the run; prints its id and page
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow         # ... and stream milestones + failures until the run ends
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Follow

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow
#>
param(
    [switch]$Follow,       # stream milestone/failure lines of the run's log until it ends
    [switch]$SkipTests,    # skip the local unit tests before packing
    [switch]$Open,         # open the run page in the browser
    [switch]$DryRun        # only show what would be packed
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)

# Lines worth seeing while a run goes: phases, scraper/analyst results, the submission, and every kind of failure.
$Milestones = 'browse done|swarm phase|site roles|brief facts|early requirements|current revision|positions,|' +
              'discount \{|materials:|verification:|submission attempt|answer \(entered|model calls:|nothing saved|' +
              'tab job failed|timed out|failed|Traceback|FATAL|CRITICAL|No lifecycle events'

if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Write-Host "== unit tests"
    $tests = cmd /c "uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q 2>&1"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $tests | Select-Object -Last 40; throw "unit tests failed: not starting a test run" }
    $tests | Select-String -Pattern '^Ran \d+ tests|^OK' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
}

if ($DryRun) {
    atira test-run . --dry-run
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

Write-Host "== starting test run"
$openFlag = if ($Open) { @() } else { @("--no-open") }
$out = (& atira test-run . @openFlag | Out-String)
Write-Host $out.Trim()
$runId = [regex]::Match($out, 'run_[0-9a-f]{16}').Value
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

Write-Host "== run $runId  https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/$runId"
if (-not $Follow) {
    Write-Host "follow its log: atira logs $runId --follow"
    exit 0
}

# cmd merges stderr into stdout without PowerShell 5.1 wrapping each stderr line as an error record.
cmd /c "atira logs $runId --follow 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match $Milestones) { $_ } }
Write-Host "== log stream of $runId ended"

lines: +# atira prints the run id on stderr: merge it in cmd (PowerShell 5.1 would turn stderr lines into errors).
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

class Tab:
    """One tab of browser `browser`, owned by one agent (one browse() at a time). `Tab(b)` is a new tab, opened at the
    first browse(); `main_tab(b)` is the tab the browser started with. Locally (no CDP) every browse() starts its own
    Chromium, so a Tab is only a label there."""

    def __init__(self, browser: int, main: bool = False):
        self.browser, self.main = browser, main
        self.target_id: str | None = None
        self.used = False            # an agent worked here before: the next browse continues from the current page

    def claim(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        self.target_id = target_id
        _OWNERS[target_id] = self

    async def open(self) -> None:
        """Create the tab now (before the session connects) so no other agent ever sees it unowned."""
        if self.target_id or self.main or not browsers.cdp_urls():
            return
        # Default: a background tab next to the others in the browser's window, so the live view's tab strip shows every
        # agent (focus emulation keeps typing and focus-dependent scripts working in it; Chrome only slows its timers).
        # TAB_WINDOWS=1: a window per tab instead (always the visible tab there, no timer slowdown, but windows hide
        # each other in the live view).
        params = {"url": "about:blank", "newWindow": True} if os.environ.get("TAB_WINDOWS") == "1" else \
            {"url": "about:blank", "background": True}
        made = await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.createTarget(params=params))
        self.claim(made["targetId"])

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the tab (never the browser's main tab)."""
        target, self.target_id = self.target_id, None
        if not target or self.main:
            return
        _OWNERS.pop(target, None)
        self.used = False
        try:
            await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.closeTarget(params={"targetId": target}))
        except Exception as error:      # already closed / browser gone
            log.debug("closing tab failed: %s", error)


def main_tab(browser: int) -> Tab:
    return _MAIN_TABS.setdefault(browser, Tab(browser, main=True))


_all_page_targets = SessionManager.get_all_page_targets


def _visible_page_targets(self) -> list:
    """What a session sees as "the browser's tabs": its own tab first, then tabs nobody owns (popups); never the tabs
    of other agents. browser-use derives its tab list, focus and new-tab reuse from this."""
    targets = _all_page_targets(self)
    tab = getattr(self.browser_session, "_tab", None)
    if tab is None:
        return targets
    return ([t for t in targets if t.target_id == tab.target_id]
            + [t for t in targets if t.target_id != tab.target_id and t.target_id not in _OWNERS])


SessionManager.get_all_page_targets = _visible_page_targets

_enable_page_monitoring = SessionManager._enable_page_monitoring


async def _enable_page_monitoring_routed(self, cdp_session) -> None:
    """browser-use registers one lifecycle handler per page target, but the CDP client keeps only ONE handler per event
    (the last one), and that handler drops events of every other target. With several tabs in a browser, navigations
    in all but the last-attached tab then waited for load events that never came (3-8 s per navigation). Here one
    handler per client routes each event to the queue of its own target."""
    await _enable_page_monitoring(self, cdp_session)

def owner_of(target_id: str) -> Tab | None:
    """The tab a target belongs to: its own claim, else the owner of the tab that opened it (popup of a popup too)."""
    seen = set()
    while target_id and target_id not in seen:
        seen.add(target_id)
        if target_id in _OWNERS:
            return _OWNERS[target_id]
        target_id = _OPENERS.get(target_id, "")
    return None

    agent's tab or popups. A tab nobody owns and no owned tab opened (the browser's first tab) is visible only to the
    browser's main tab, which claims it. browser-use derives its tab list, focus and new-tab reuse from this."""
    targets = _all_page_targets(self)
    tab = getattr(self.browser_session, "_tab", None)
    if tab is None:
        return targets
    mine = [t for t in targets if t.target_id == tab.target_id]
    rest = [t for t in targets if t.target_id != tab.target_id
            and (owner_of(t.target_id) is tab or (owner_of(t.target_id) is None and tab.main))]

TASK = {"brief": "b", "access": [{"siteId": "erp", "url": "http://x", "credentials": {}}],
        "submission": {"kind": "api"}, "expires_at": None}


class BoardTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_post_query_and_wait(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        waiter = asyncio.create_task(board.wait_for(kind="a.b", timeout=2))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        await board.post(Evidence("a.b", "erp", {"x": 1}, source="u"))
        self.assertEqual((await waiter)[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(board.query("a", prefix=True)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(board.query("a.b", site="mail"), [])

    async def test_dump_and_load_round_trip(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        await board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {"x": 1}))
        await board.set("r", [1])
        path = Path(__file__).parent / "_board.json"
        try:
            board.dump(path)
            again = Blackboard.load(path)
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(again.evidence[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(again.get("r"), [1])


class ParseJson(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fenced_and_chatty(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_json('Sure!\n```json\n{"a": [1, 2]}\n```'), {"a": [1, 2]})

    def test_garbage_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_json("no json here")


def make_agents(order):
    class Boom(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self): raise RuntimeError("boom")

    class Collect(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("collect")
            await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {}))

    class Analyze(Agent):
        phase = Phase.ANALYZE
        async def run(self):
            order.append(f"analyze sees {len(self.ctx.board.query('k'))}")

    class Submit(Agent):
        phase = Phase.SUBMIT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("submit")
            await self.ctx.board.set("answer", {"ok": True})

    return [Submit, Analyze, Boom, Collect]


class Orchestration(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_with(self, classes, task=TASK, env=None):
        with patch.object(orchestrator, "discover", lambda: classes):
            return await orchestrator.run_swarm(task, None, scored=True, env=env or {})

    async def test_phases_run_in_order_and_a_failure_does_not_stop_the_rest(self):
        order = []
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order))
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "analyze sees 1", "submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    async def test_site_submission_returns_nothing_to_post(self):
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents([]), task={**TASK, "submission": {"kind": "site"}})
        self.assertIsNone(answer)

    async def test_only_filter(self):
        order = []
        await self.run_with(make_agents(order), env={"SWARM_ONLY": "Collect,Submit"})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "submit"])

    async def test_out_of_time_skips_work_but_still_submits(self):
        order = []
        late = {**TASK, "expires_at": (time.time() + 100) * 1000}   # inside the submit margin
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order), task=late)
        self.assertEqual(order, ["submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    def test_only_task_sites_are_allowed_and_telemetry_is_off(self):
        import os
        from swarm import browser_agent
        task = {"access": [{"url": "https://a.example/x?y=1"}, {"url": "http://b.example:8080/"}, {"url": ""}]}
        self.assertEqual(browser_agent.allowed_domains(task), ["https://a.example", "http://b.example:8080"])
        for flag in ("ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY", "BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC", "BROWSER_USE_VERSION_CHECK"):

        self.assertIs(AboutBlankWatchdog._show_dvd_screensaver_loading_animation_cdp,

class BrowseTools(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_our_actions_are_registered_and_helpers_are_not(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        tools = browser_agent.build_tools(None, "erp", "t", None)
        names = set(tools.registry.registry.actions)
        self.assertTrue({"record", "read_page", "fill_form"} <= names)
        self.assertNotIn("read_one", names)

    def test_unused_browser_use_actions_are_excluded(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        names = set(browser_agent.build_tools(None, "erp", "t", None).registry.registry.actions)
        self.assertFalse(set(browser_agent.EXCLUDED_ACTIONS) & names)
        self.assertTrue({"navigate", "click", "input", "done"} <= names)

    def test_flash_prompt_formats(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        text = browser_agent.FLASH_SYSTEM.format(max_actions=4)
        self.assertIn("Max 4 actions", text)
        self.assertIn('{"memory"', text)


class Tabs(unittest.TestCase):
    def tearDown(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        browser_agent._OWNERS.clear()

    def test_agent_sees_own_tab_first_and_never_other_agents_tabs(self):
        from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
        from swarm import browser_agent
        mine, other = browser_agent.Tab(0), browser_agent.Tab(0)
        mine.claim("t-mine")
        other.claim("t-other")
        targets = [NS(target_id=t, target_type="page") for t in ("t-popup", "t-other", "t-mine")]
        manager = NS(_targets={t.target_id: t for t in targets}, browser_session=NS(_tab=mine))
        seen = [t.target_id for t in browser_agent._visible_page_targets(manager)]
        self.assertEqual(seen, ["t-mine", "t-popup"])
        manager.browser_session = NS(_tab=None)            # sessions without a tab see everything
        self.assertEqual(len(browser_agent._visible_page_targets(manager)), 3)

The second run (`run_e05860efa33b5cc8`) finished collecting much faster, but its ERP results are wrong. I found the cause, fixed it, and started a third test run with the fix.

**Results from `run_e05860efa33b5cc8`**
- Collection finished in 7:44, against 23:45 in the run before the speed changes.
- There were no "No lifecycle events" warnings, so the page-load fix works.
- Several ERP agents ended up in the same browser tab, the one with the id ending DD39. They typed over each other ("search field kept reverting to GR-6617…", "Node does not belong to the document").
- As a result, only 1 of 5 positions got a material (01.01), and its status wasn't read; 01.02–01.05 have none. So this run is fast, but the bid will be mostly empty.

**Cause:** a tab that no agent owned was visible to every agent in the browser. That covers tabs a site opens itself (`target=_blank`) and tabs an agent opens. DD39 was one of these. The agents could see it was already logged in with the search open, so they all switched into it.

**Fix** (`swarm/browser_agent.py`):
- The code now records which tab opened which, using Chrome's own tab info. A tab another tab opened belongs to that tab's agent, and only that agent sees it.
- When an agent moves into such a tab, it becomes that agent's tab and is closed together with its main tab.
- A tab that nobody opened (such as the browser's first tab) is visible only to that browser's main agent.
- Two new unit tests cover this, and all 46 tests pass. I also re-ran the local headless check: each session still saw only its own tab.

**The test-run script** had a bug: `atira test-run` prints the run id on the error stream, which the script didn't capture. That's fixed. The third run was started with the script, so its monitor will show whether the fix works ("== run …" or "no run id").

**Runs now in progress:**
- `run_d1ee764b7577c7dc`: the first version, still running as you asked.
- `run_e05860efa33b5cc8`: now in the bid-submission phase.
- The third run, with the tab-ownership fix: its id arrives with the first monitor event.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent**
   - Speed up the Atira EHL RFQ agent swarm without losing quality. Inputs to the speed work:
     - The user's idea of HTML for extraction plus vision for clicks; it was already effectively the case, since screenshots were off.
     - The user's 3-point plan:
       1. Compress instructions and other text sent to the model using the caveman skill at a high setting, cutting input tokens without losing information.
       2. Use parallel tabs and make sure no tab is left unused.
       3. Use flash_mode for models that only extract and navigate; keep thinking for orchestration models that make important decisions.
   - Run test runs in the background with monitoring, and keep working while waiting.
   - Inspect why tabs were "not working / not opening".
   - Put tabs side by side in one window, and write a small script that starts a test run the way I launched it before.
   - "do not cancel. Start new run alongside": never cancel running test runs without being asked.
   - Additional summary instruction: store knowledge about how agents collect data and their pain points (section 5).

2. **Key Technical Concepts**
   - Atira platform:
     - Scored runs last 20 min; test runs up to 2 h, unscored.
     - Hosted Qwen (`qwen3.8-flash-next`): 32 concurrent calls; calls carry a queue wait.
     - Max 4 browsers over CDP; tabs are unlimited.
     - Fair play: no scenario values in the package; the model must choose where to go; no fixed scripts.
   - Swarm architecture: blackboard, phases COLLECT → VERIFY → COMPUTE → SUBMIT, scrapers per site role, analysts that extract with JSON shapes, `done.*` flags.
   - browser-use 0.11.13:
     - `Agent` params: `flash_mode`, `override_system_message`, `extend_system_message`, `directly_open_url`, `max_actions_per_step`.
     - `Tools(exclude_actions=...)`, `BrowserSession` (pydantic, `PrivateAttr`), `SessionManager`.
   - cdp_use `CDPClient`: registry keeps ONE handler per event method, and the last one registered wins.
   - CDP calls used:
     - `Target.createTarget` (`background` / `newWindow`), `Target.closeTarget`
     - `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`
     - `TargetInfo.openerId`
   - Chrome: background-tab timer throttling; focus problems in windows that don't have the OS focus.
   - atira CLI and MCP tools: `test_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`, `run_screenshot`, `run_inputs`, `get_run`, `list_runs`.

3. **Files and Code Sections**

   **`swarm/browser_agent.py`** (core; heavily modified)
   - Module docstring now describes `Tab`, the one-browse()-per-tab rule, and flash mode.
   - Imports added: `httpx`, `SessionManager`, `CDPClient`, `PrivateAttr`, `Any`, `urlunparse`.
   - `FLASH_SYSTEM`: compact flash system prompt, formatted with `max_actions`; reply JSON is `{"memory": ..., "action": [...]}`.
   - `SYSTEM_EXTRA`: rewritten in caveman style. Same rules (cookie walls, `read_page`, `fill_form`, traps, never invent values), plus "Tabs you did not open belong to other agents: never switch to or close them."

"""The swarm framework against fakes: blackboard, JSON parsing, phase orchestration, failure isolation."""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from swarm import Agent, Blackboard, Evidence, Phase  # noqa: E402
from swarm import orchestrator  # noqa: E402
from swarm.llm import parse_json  # noqa: E402

TASK = {"brief": "b", "access": [{"siteId": "erp", "url": "http://x", "credentials": {}}],
        "submission": {"kind": "api"}, "expires_at": None}


class BoardTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_post_query_and_wait(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        waiter = asyncio.create_task(board.wait_for(kind="a.b", timeout=2))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        await board.post(Evidence("a.b", "erp", {"x": 1}, source="u"))
        self.assertEqual((await waiter)[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(board.query("a", prefix=True)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(board.query("a.b", site="mail"), [])

    async def test_dump_and_load_round_trip(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        await board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {"x": 1}))
        await board.set("r", [1])
        path = Path(__file__).parent / "_board.json"
        try:
            board.dump(path)
            again = Blackboard.load(path)
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(again.evidence[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(again.get("r"), [1])


class ParseJson(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fenced_and_chatty(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_json('Sure!\n```json\n{"a": [1, 2]}\n```'), {"a": [1, 2]})

    def test_garbage_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_json("no json here")


def make_agents(order):
    class Boom(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self): raise RuntimeError("boom")

    class Collect(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("collect")
            await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {}))

    class Analyze(Agent):
        phase = Phase.ANALYZE
        async def run(self):
            order.append(f"analyze sees {len(self.ctx.board.query('k'))}")

    class Submit(Agent):
        phase = Phase.SUBMIT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("submit")
            await self.ctx.board.set("answer", {"ok": True})

    return [Submit, Analyze, Boom, Collect]


class Orchestration(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_with(self, classes, task=TASK, env=None):
        with patch.object(orchestrator, "discover", lambda: classes):
            return await orchestrator.run_swarm(task, None, scored=True, env=env or {})

    async def test_phases_run_in_order_and_a_failure_does_not_stop_the_rest(self):
        order = []
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order))
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "analyze sees 1", "submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    async def test_site_submission_returns_nothing_to_post(self):
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents([]), task={**TASK, "submission": {"kind": "site"}})
        self.assertIsNone(answer)

    async def test_only_filter(self):
        order = []
        await self.run_with(make_agents(order), env={"SWARM_ONLY": "Collect,Submit"})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "submit"])

    async def test_out_of_time_skips_work_but_still_submits(self):
        order = []
        late = {**TASK, "expires_at": (time.time() + 100) * 1000}   # inside the submit margin
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order), task=late)
        self.assertEqual(order, ["submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

class Tabs(unittest.TestCase):
    def tearDown(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        browser_agent._OWNERS.clear()
        browser_agent._OPENERS.clear()

    def test_agent_sees_own_tab_and_its_popups_never_other_agents_tabs(self):
        from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
        from swarm import browser_agent
        main, mine, other = browser_agent.Tab(0, main=True), browser_agent.Tab(0), browser_agent.Tab(0)
        main.claim("t-main")
        mine.claim("t-mine")
        other.claim("t-other")
        browser_agent._OPENERS.update({"t-my-popup": "t-mine", "t-its-popup": "t-other"})
        ids = ("t-stray", "t-its-popup", "t-other", "t-my-popup", "t-main", "t-mine")
        manager = NS(_targets={t: NS(target_id=t, target_type="page") for t in ids}, browser_session=NS(_tab=mine))
        seen = lambda tab: [t.target_id for t in browser_agent._visible_page_targets(  # noqa: E731
            NS(_targets=manager._targets, browser_session=NS(_tab=tab)))]
        self.assertEqual(seen(mine), ["t-mine", "t-my-popup"])
        self.assertEqual(seen(other), ["t-other", "t-its-popup"])
        self.assertEqual(seen(main), ["t-main", "t-stray"])      # a tab nobody opened: only the main tab sees it
        self.assertEqual(len(seen(None)), 6)                     # sessions without a tab see everything

    def test_focused_popup_is_adopted_and_closed_with_the_tab(self):
        from swarm import browser_agent
        mine, other = browser_agent.Tab(0), browser_agent.Tab(0)
        mine.claim("t-mine")
        other.claim("t-other")
        mine.adopt("t-new")
        mine.adopt("t-other")                                    # never another agent's tab
        self.assertIs(browser_agent.owner_of("t-new"), mine)
        self.assertIs(browser_agent.owner_of("t-other"), other)
        self.assertEqual(mine.popups, {"t-new"})


class RealAgentsImport(unittest.TestCase):

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Start a sandbox test run of this package (public data, unscored) and optionally follow its key log lines.

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1                 # unit tests, then start the run; prints its id and page
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -Follow         # ... and stream milestones + failures until the run ends
  .\scripts\test-run.ps1 -SkipTests -Follow

  From Git Bash / a Claude Code Monitor:
  powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-run.ps1 -Follow
#>
param(
    [switch]$Follow,       # stream milestone/failure lines of the run's log until it ends
    [switch]$SkipTests,    # skip the local unit tests before packing
    [switch]$Open,         # open the run page in the browser
    [switch]$DryRun        # only show what would be packed
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)

# Lines worth seeing while a run goes: phases, scraper/analyst results, the submission, and every kind of failure.
$Milestones = 'browse done|swarm phase|site roles|brief facts|early requirements|current revision|positions,|' +
              'discount \{|materials:|verification:|submission attempt|answer \(entered|model calls:|nothing saved|' +
              'tab job failed|timed out|failed|Traceback|FATAL|CRITICAL|No lifecycle events'

if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Write-Host "== unit tests"
    $tests = cmd /c "uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q 2>&1"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $tests | Select-Object -Last 40; throw "unit tests failed: not starting a test run" }
    $tests | Select-String -Pattern '^Ran \d+ tests|^OK' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
}

if ($DryRun) {
    atira test-run . --dry-run
    exit $LASTEXITCODE
}

Write-Host "== starting test run"
$openFlag = if ($Open) { "" } else { "--no-open" }
# atira prints the run id on stderr: merge it in cmd (PowerShell 5.1 would turn stderr lines into errors).
$out = (cmd /c "atira test-run . $openFlag 2>&1" | Out-String)
Write-Host $out.Trim()
$runId = [regex]::Match($out, 'run_[0-9a-f]{16}').Value
if (-not $runId) { throw "no run id in the atira output" }

Write-Host "== run $runId  https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/$runId"
if (-not $Follow) {
    Write-Host "follow its log: atira logs $runId --follow"
    exit 0
}

# cmd merges stderr into stdout without PowerShell 5.1 wrapping each stderr line as an error record.
cmd /c "atira logs $runId --follow 2>&1" | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -match $Milestones) { $_ } }
Write-Host "== log stream of $runId ended"
