tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: scraper   SITE: our ERP (role "erp")
"""Looks up ERP candidates for the required cylinders, saved as page evidence ("erp.page").

The ERP only lists records for narrow searches, so the work starts once the requirements are known
(results["requirements"], from agents/analyze_requirements.py): one work item per catalogue group (Kataloggruppe).
While waiting, the main tab of browser 2 logs in and passes the ERP's gates. Then up to ERP_TABS workers (the main tab
plus new tabs of the same browser, which share the login) take items from a shared queue until it is empty; a worker
closes its tab when the queue is empty, so no tab sits idle. results["done.erp"] is set when every item has been worked on.
"""
import asyncio

from swarm import Phase, register  # noqa: F401
from swarm.browser_agent import Tab
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
from swarm.scraper import SiteScraper
from swarm.sites import site_for

ANALYSIS_TIME_S = 120    # what the material matcher needs after the last ERP page
ERP_TABS = 5             # parallel ERP workers at most (main tab included)

HINTS = ("ERP habits: SAP-style transaction codes (start page / menu lists transactions for material display, stock "
         "overview, price conditions); system notice or access gate after login (copy displayed number exactly - "
         "read_page shows numbers drawn on canvas -, confirm, continue; slider/robot gate passes with ONE fill_form: "
         "slider = its maximum (e.g. 100), robot checkbox = true, then the number and confirmation checkbox, then_click "
         "continue button); material search help (F4) lists results only for narrow search term; records with several "
         "tabs/registers (basic data, technical data, planning/status with lead times; condition header and quantity "
         "scales; stock per plant and per storage location); status codes explained in legend or tooltip; short session "
         "timeout - log in again when login page appears. Save steps: once you see the links of a record's "
         "tabs/registers, read all with ONE read_page(urls=[...]); use same URL pattern for next candidate.")


def work_items(requirements: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """One item per catalogue group (or per requirement when no group is given), with the attributes to check."""
    items: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for ref, req in (requirements or {}).items():
        group = (req.get("kataloggruppe") or "").strip()
        key = group or f"req:{ref}"
        item = items.setdefault(key, {"group": group, "requirements": []})
        item["requirements"].append({k: req.get(k) for k in ("bore", "stroke", "stroke_kind", "pressure", "mounting",
                                                              "certification")} | {"ref": ref})
    return list(items.values())


def item_goal(item: dict) -> str:
    reqs = "\n".join(f"- requirement {r['ref']}: bore {r['bore']} mm, stroke {r['stroke']} mm"
                     f"{' (usable travel; nominal stroke will be longer)' if r.get('stroke_kind') == 'usable' else ''}, "
                     f"pressure {r['pressure']} bar, mounting {r['mounting']}, certification {r['certification']}"
                     for r in item["requirements"])
    what = f"catalogue group (Kataloggruppe) {item['group']}" if item["group"] else "these technical attributes"
    return (
        f"Find our ERP materials for {what}. Required:\n{reqs}\n"
        "1. Log in if needed, open material search (search help of material display transaction). Search "
        f"{item['group'] or 'the attributes'}, read_page result list with topic 'erp search {item['group']}'.\n"
        "2. Candidates = results whose bore, pressure, mounting, certification match (stroke may differ slightly; keep "
        "candidates with any stroke). Each candidate: open material record, read_page EVERY tab (technical data; "
        "planning/status with lead times) with topic 'erp material <number>'.\n"
        "3. Each candidate with status active/released (not blocked): read_page its price conditions with "
        "quantity-scale register open (topic 'erp prices <number>'); several condition records -> next_page_link = "
        "exact text of link to next condition record, so all read. Then read_page its stock: open storage-location "
        "level and freely usable location so quantity shows (topic 'erp stock <number>').\n"
        "Do not stop after first candidate. done listing candidates and their status.")


async def _queue(ctx):
    async with ctx.lock("erp.queue"):
        if "erp.queue" not in ctx.shared:
            requirements = await ctx.board.wait_for(key="requirements", timeout=max(1.0, ctx.time_left()))
            used = {str(p.get("requirement_ref") or "").strip().upper()
                    for p in ((ctx.board.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or [])}
            if used - {""}:                       # only requirements some position refers to
                requirements = {k: v for k, v in requirements.items() if k.strip().upper() in used} or requirements
            items = work_items(requirements)
            queue = asyncio.Queue()
            for item in items:
                queue.put_nowait(item)
            ctx.shared["erp.queue"] = queue
            ctx.shared["erp.pending"] = len(items)
            await ctx.board.set("erp.work_items", items)
        return ctx.shared["erp.queue"]


@register
class ErpScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "erp"
    browser = 2
    max_steps = 30
    hints = HINTS

    async def work(self, queue: asyncio.Queue, tab: Tab | None = None) -> None:
        """Take items until the queue is empty (or time is up); `tab` None = the main tab."""
        while self.ctx.time_left() > ANALYSIS_TIME_S:
            try:
                item = queue.get_nowait()
            except asyncio.QueueEmpty:
                return
            try:   # stop browsing early enough for the matcher to extract and match before collecting ends
                await self.browse_until_done(item_goal(item), attempts=2, tab=tab,
                                             stop_reserve=SUBMIT_RESERVE_S + ANALYSIS_TIME_S)
            except Exception as error:
                self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"{item.get('group')}: {error}")
            finally:
                self.ctx.shared["erp.pending"] -= 1
                if self.ctx.shared["erp.pending"] <= 0:
                    await self.ctx.board.set("done.erp", True)

    async def tab_worker(self, queue: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
        tab = Tab(self.browser)
        try:
            await self.work(queue, tab)
        finally:
            await tab.close()

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            if self.ctx.board.get("requirements") is None:      # use the wait: log in and pass the ERP's gates now
                await self.browse("Log in, accept cookies, pass any system notice or access gate, open material search "
                                  "help of material display transaction. Do NOT search yet. done once search form open.",
                                  max_steps=12)
            queue = await _queue(self.ctx)
            extra = max(0, min(ERP_TABS, queue.qsize()) - 1)
            await asyncio.gather(self.work(queue), *(self.tab_worker(queue) for _ in range(extra)))
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.erp", True)

    "at a time ('<reference> <topic>'). Search inbox AND archive folder (page through results). Look-alike references "
    "(same reference with suffix) and other tenders do not count; drafts, previews, superseded mails look similar: "
    "read each candidate message.\n"
    "Every message whose subject or text names this tender's reference and the topic: read_page it with topic "
    "'<topic> mail' - several selected messages at once with read_page(urls=[their links]) - (read_page also reads "
    "collapsed or locked parts, no need to unlock). Reading pane shows no message text -> open message's own page "
    "('open original'/message link) and read that. Skip signing-TAN mails.")


@register
class MailScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "mail"
    browser = 3
    max_steps = 26
    hints = ("Webmail habits: cookie wall after login; maintenance popups (close them, never follow their links); "
             "search may sit behind slider/robot gate: first try ONE fill_form (slider = its maximum, robot checkbox = "
             "true); still locked -> focus the slider and press End, or click its right end; never loop on evaluate; "
             "inbox and archive folder; paged result lists; message headers "
             "(sender, date) in collapsed 'envelope/headers' section, which read_page includes.")

    async def login(self) -> None:
        """Log in once in the main tab, so the topic tabs start logged in (they would log in themselves otherwise)."""
        try:
            await self.browse("Log in, accept cookie wall, close popups, open inbox. Do NOT search yet. Then done.",
                              max_steps=8)
        except Exception as error:
            self.log.warning("login browse failed: %s", error)

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            facts, _ = await asyncio.gather(self.wait_brief(), self.login())
            facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or facts
            discount = (f"Find discount approvals for this tender (sender: "
                        f"{facts.get('director_sender') or 'the sales director'}). Topic words to try: "
                        f"{facts.get('discount_topic') or 'Rabatt'}, Rabattfreigabe.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            rules = ("Find condition-rule mails (Konditionsregeln) and technical release mails (Technikfreigabe) for "
                     f"this tender, if they exist, one search per topic.\n{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done.")
            topics = [t for t in (facts.get("mail_topics") or []) if t and t.lower() not in CORE_TOPICS]
            groups = [topics[i:i + TOPICS_PER_TAB] for i in range(0, len(topics), TOPICS_PER_TAB)]
            if len(groups) > MAX_REST_TABS:            # keep the tab count bounded: spread the topics evenly
                groups = [topics[i::MAX_REST_TABS] for i in range(MAX_REST_TABS)]
            rest = [f"Find release mails for this tender on these topics, one search per topic: {', '.join(g)}.\n"
                    f"{SEARCH_RULES}\nThen done." for g in groups]

            async def core() -> None:
                outs = await asyncio.gather(self.browse_until_done(discount, attempts=2),
                                            self.browse_in_tabs([rules], max_steps=26))
                await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", outs[0]["summary"])
                await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)

            await asyncio.gather(core(), self.browse_in_tabs(rest, max_steps=26) if rest else asyncio.sleep(0))
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail_core", True)
            await self.ctx.board.set("done.mail", True)

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: analyst   NEEDS: erp.page (done.erp), results["requirements"], results["tender"], results["mail"]
# WRITES: results["erp"], results["materials"]
"""Turns the saved ERP pages into materials, price conditions and stock, then matches each position in code:
an ACTIVE material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all equal the requirement exactly.
A requirement given as usable travel (nutzbarer Weg) gets twice the per-end reserve of the technical release for the
current revision added (amendments were already applied by the requirement analyst).

results["erp"] = {"materials": {no: {...}}, "conditions": [{...}], "stock": {no: {"free": "12", "locations": [...]}}}
results["materials"] = {position: {"material": no | None, "required": {...}, "candidates": [...], "reason": str}}
"""
import asyncio
import re
from decimal import Decimal

from swarm import Agent, Phase, register
from swarm.extract import extract, page_block, pages
from swarm.normalize import norm_ref, to_decimal

MATERIAL_SHAPE = """{"materials": [{"material": "material number", "description": "", "kataloggruppe": "",
  "bore": "", "stroke": "", "pressure": "", "mounting": "", "certification": "",
  "status_code": "as shown", "status_meaning": "meaning from the legend/tooltip",
  "is_active": "true/false from the status and its legend, or null if no status is shown for this material",
  "lead_time_stock_weeks": "", "lead_time_production_weeks": "", "pieces_per_carton": "",
  "allocation_mass_g": "allocation/Umlage weight per piece in g", "surcharge_mass_g": "surcharge mass per piece in g",
  "metal_index": "price index code"}]}"""

CONDITION_SHAPE = """{"conditions": [{"material": "", "record": "condition record no./page", "condition_type": "",
  "valid_from": "as shown", "valid_to": "as shown", "currency": "", "fx_key": null,
  "price_unit": "price unit quantity, e.g. 100", "number_format": "e.g. en-US or de-DE if stated",
  "scales": [{"min_qty": "as shown incl. locale marker", "price": "as shown incl. locale marker"}]}]}"""

STOCK_SHAPE = """{"stock": [{"material": "", "plant": "", "location": "", "quantity": "as shown",
  "usable": "true if freely usable (unrestricted), false if blocked/quality inspection/not available"}]}"""

MATERIAL_INSTRUCTION = ("List every ERP material on these pages with all attributes (merge tabs of one material). "
                        "is_active true only if status legend says released/active (not blocked).")
CONDITION_INSTRUCTION = ("List every price condition record on these pages with all quantity-scale rows. Keep number "
                         "strings exactly with locale markers; note stated number format.")
STOCK_INSTRUCTION = ("List stock quantities per material and storage location on these pages. Plant total including "
                     "blocked/inspection stock NOT usable; usable=true only for freely usable storage-location stock.")


def num(text, locale=None) -> Decimal | None:
    return to_decimal(text, locale)


def same(a, b) -> bool:
    x, y = num(a), num(b)
    if x is not None and y is not None:
        return x == y
    return norm_ref(a) == norm_ref(b) and norm_ref(a) != ""


_NONE = re.compile(r"^(KEINE?|NONE|OHNE|NICHT|N/?A|—|-|–)")


def text_equal(a, b) -> bool:
    """Equal after normalisation; 'none required' and 'none' count as the same (no certification)."""
    x, y = norm_ref(a), norm_ref(b)
    if _NONE.match(x) and _NONE.match(y):
        return True
    return x == y and x != ""


def merge_materials(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    out: dict = {}
    for r in rows:
        no = norm_ref(r.get("material"))
        if not no:
            continue
        cur = out.setdefault(no, {"material": str(r.get("material")).strip()})
        for k, v in r.items():
            if v not in (None, "", "null") and (cur.get(k) in (None, "") or k == "is_active" and v is False):
                cur[k] = v
    return out


def required_stroke(req: dict, mail: dict, current_revision: str) -> Decimal | None:
    stroke = num(req.get("stroke"))
    if stroke is None or req.get("stroke_kind") != "usable":
        return stroke
    releases = (mail or {}).get("technical_release") or {}
    key = norm_ref(req.get("reserve_key"))
    match = releases.get(key) if key else None
    if match is None:
        same_rev = [r for r in releases.values() if norm_ref(r.get("revision")) == norm_ref(current_revision)]
        match = same_rev[0] if len(same_rev) == 1 else None
    reserve = num((match or {}).get("reserve_mm_per_end"))
    return stroke + 2 * reserve if reserve is not None else None


def match_positions(tender: dict, requirements: dict, materials: dict, mail: dict, current: str) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for p in (tender or {}).get("positions") or []:
        pos = str(p.get("position")).strip()
        ref = next((r for r in requirements if norm_ref(r) == norm_ref(p.get("requirement_ref"))), None)
        req = requirements.get(ref) if ref else None
        if not req:
            out[pos] = {"material": None, "reason": f"requirement {p.get('requirement_ref')} not found", "candidates": []}
            continue
        stroke = required_stroke(req, mail, current)
        group = norm_ref(req.get("kataloggruppe"))
        cands = []
        for m in materials.values():
            if group and norm_ref(m.get("kataloggruppe")) and norm_ref(m.get("kataloggruppe")) != group:
                continue
            ok = (same(m.get("bore"), req.get("bore")) and stroke is not None and num(m.get("stroke")) == stroke
                  and same(m.get("pressure"), req.get("pressure")) and text_equal(m.get("mounting"), req.get("mounting"))
                  and text_equal(m.get("certification"), req.get("certification")))
            if ok:
                active = m.get("is_active")
                cands.append({"material": m["material"], "status": m.get("status_code"),
                              "active": True if active in (True, "true") else False if active in (False, "false") else None})
        active = [c for c in cands if c["active"] is True]
        unknown = [c for c in cands if c["active"] is None]       # status page not read: better than nothing
        required = {k: req.get(k) for k in ("bore", "pressure", "mounting", "certification", "kataloggruppe")}
        required["stroke"] = None if stroke is None else format(stroke.normalize(), "f")
        chosen = active or unknown
        out[pos] = {"material": chosen[0]["material"] if chosen else None, "required": required, "candidates": cands,
                    "reason": "exact active match" if active else "exact match, status not read" if unknown else
                    ("only blocked matches" if cands else "no exact match among the ERP records read")}
    return out


@register
class MaterialMatcher(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT

    async def run(self) -> None:
        await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="done.erp", timeout=max(1.0, self.ctx.time_left()))
        blocks = [page_block(e) for e in pages(self.ctx, "erp")]
        if not blocks:
            raise RuntimeError("no ERP pages were saved")
        mats, conds, stock_out = await asyncio.gather(
            extract(self.ctx, MATERIAL_INSTRUCTION, MATERIAL_SHAPE, blocks, list_key="materials", chunk_size=25_000),
            extract(self.ctx, CONDITION_INSTRUCTION, CONDITION_SHAPE, blocks, list_key="conditions", chunk_size=25_000),
            extract(self.ctx, STOCK_INSTRUCTION, STOCK_SHAPE, blocks, list_key="stock", chunk_size=25_000))
        materials = merge_materials(mats.get("materials") or [])
        stock: dict = {}
        for s in stock_out.get("stock") or []:           # one row per (material, location); a re-read replaces
            stock.setdefault(norm_ref(s.get("material")), {})[norm_ref(s.get("location")) or norm_ref(s.get("plant"))] = s
        for no, rows in list(stock.items()):
            free = sum((num(s.get("quantity")) or Decimal(0) for s in rows.values()
                        if str(s.get("usable")).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")), Decimal(0))
            stock[no] = {"free": free, "locations": list(rows.values())}
        erp = {"materials": materials, "conditions": conds.get("conditions") or [],
               "stock": {k: {"free": format(v["free"], "f"), "locations": v["locations"]} for k, v in stock.items()}}
        await self.ctx.board.set("erp", erp)
        try:
            await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="requirements_final", timeout=max(1.0, min(90, self.ctx.time_left())))
            await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="mail", timeout=max(1.0, min(90, self.ctx.time_left())))  # end reserves
        except TimeoutError:
            self.log.warning("matching without final requirements or mail")
        mail =self.ctx.board.get("mail") or {}
        spec = self.ctx.board.get("spec") or {}
        result = match_positions(self.ctx.board.get("tender") or {}, self.ctx.board.get("requirements") or {},
                                 materials, mail, spec.get("current", ""))
        await self.ctx.board.set("materials", result)
        self.log.info("materials: %s", {p: (r["material"], r["reason"]) for p, r in result.items()})

1	"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.
2	
3	Subclass, set `role` ('tender' | 'spec' | 'erp' | 'mail') and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should
4	find, in general terms derived from the brief; never scenario values). The site id for the role is resolved at run
5	time (datasets name their sites differently). Override `run()` for several browse passes; call `self.browse(goal)`.
6	
7	When the scraper ends (done, failed or out of time) it sets results[f"done.{role}"] so analysts waiting on it start.
8	Independent jobs run at once with `browse_in_tabs` (one new tab each, closed when its job ends); `self.browse` works
9	in the browser's main tab.
10	"""
11	import asyncio
12	
13	from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
14	from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
15	from swarm.browser_agent import Tab, browse
16	from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
17	from swarm.extract import brief_intro
18	from swarm.sites import site_for
19	
20	
21	class SiteScraper(Agent):
22	    phase = Phase.COLLECT
23	    role: str = ""
24	    site_id: str = ""
25	    max_steps: int = 40
26	    hints: str = ""
27	
28	    def goal(self) -> str:
29	        raise NotImplementedError
30	
31	    def login_text(self) -> str:
32	        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
33	        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `role` ('tender' | 'spec' | 'erp' | 'mail') and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should
find, in general terms derived from the brief; never scenario values). The site id for the role is resolved at run
time (datasets name their sites differently). Override `run()` for several browse passes; call `self.browse(goal)`.

When the scraper ends (done, failed or out of time) it sets results[f"done.{role}"] so analysts waiting on it start.
Independent jobs run at once with `browse_in_tabs` (one new tab each, closed when its job ends); `self.browse` works
in the browser's main tab.
"""
import asyncio

from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import Tab, browse
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
from swarm.extract import brief_intro
from swarm.sites import site_for


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    role: str = ""
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}
        return f"Site ({self.role}): {site['url']}\nLogin: username {creds.get('username')!r}, password {creds.get('password')!r}"

    def task_text(self) -> str:
        facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or {}
        known = {k: facts.get(k) for k in ("tender_reference", "tender_title", "buyer", "scenario_date", "bidder_company")
                 if facts.get(k)}
        return f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}\nKey facts: {known}" if known else \
            f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        kind = f"{self.role}.page" if rec["kind"] == "page" else rec["kind"]
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=kind, site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"], source=rec["source"],
                                           author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def browse(self, job: str, *, browser: int | None = None, max_steps: int | None = None, **kwargs) -> dict:
        prompt = "\n\n".join([self.login_text(), self.task_text(), f"YOUR JOB:\n{job}"])
        out = await browse(self.ctx, prompt, browser=self.browser if browser is None else browser, site_id=self.site_id,
                           on_record=self.post, max_steps=max_steps or self.max_steps, hints=self.hints,
                           author=self.name, **kwargs)
        self.log.info("browse done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:300])
        return out

    async def browse_until_done(self, job: str, attempts: int = 3, **kwargs) -> dict:
        """browse(); if the agent stopped without finishing (errors, step limit), start again with a note on what
        is already saved, while time allows."""
        out = {"summary": "", "done": False}
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            note = ""
            if attempt:
                saved = sorted({e.data.get("topic") for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page")} - {None})
                note = (f"\n\nNOTE: previous attempt stopped early ({out['summary'][:300]!r}). Already saved: "
                        f"{saved or 'nothing'}. Do only what is missing.")
            out = await self.browse(job + note, **kwargs)
            if out["done"] or self.ctx.seconds_left() - kwargs.get("stop_reserve", SUBMIT_RESERVE_S) < 120:
                break
        return out

    async def browse_in_tabs(self, jobs: list[str], *, browser: int | None = None, attempts: int = 2,
                             **kwargs) -> list[dict]:
        """Run `jobs` at once, each in a new tab of this scraper's browser (the tabs share its login cookies). Each tab
        is closed as soon as its job ends, so no tab sits idle. A failed job returns {"summary": error, "done": False}."""
        async def one(job: str) -> dict:
            tab = Tab(self.browser if browser is None else browser)
            try:
                return await self.browse_until_done(job, attempts=attempts, tab=tab, **kwargs)
            except Exception as error:
                self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"tab job failed: {error}")
                return {"summary": str(error), "done": False}
            finally:
                await tab.close()
        return list(await asyncio.gather(*(one(job) for job in jobs)))

    async def wait_brief(self, timeout: float = 180) -> dict:
        try:
            return await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="brief", timeout=timeout) or {}
        except TimeoutError:
            return {}

    def required(self) -> list[tuple[tuple[str, ...], str]]:
        """Pages that must be saved, as (topic keywords, focused job). After the main browse, a focused browse runs
        for each one whose keywords appear in no saved topic. Override per scraper."""
        return []

    def saved_topics(self) -> str:
        return " | ".join(str(e.data.get("topic", "")).lower() for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page"))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            out = await self.browse_until_done(self.goal())   # the brief's intro already names the tender: start at once
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            for keywords, job in self.required():
                if self.ctx.time_left() > 90 and not any(k in self.saved_topics() for k in keywords):
                    self.log.warning("nothing saved for %s: focused browse", keywords)
                    await self.browse(job, max_steps=15)
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"done.{self.role}", True)

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: scraper   SITE: tender portal (role "tender")
"""Reads the tender: overview, bill of quantities and ALL bidder Q&A, saved as page evidence ("tender.page").
Analysts turn the pages into positions, quantities, amendments and commercial keys (agents/analyze_quantities.py).

The main tab logs in and opens the tender; then the documents (main tab) and the Q&A (a second tab, sharing the
login) are read at the same time."""
import asyncio

from swarm import Phase, register  # noqa: F401
from swarm.scraper import SiteScraper
from swarm.sites import site_for

QA_JOB = ("Open this tender's bidder questions/answers (Q&A, Bieterfragen) and read_page them with topic 'bidder Q&A' "
          "and next_page_link = exact text of next-page link, so every page read in one action. Then done.")
DOCS_JOB = ("Open this tender's documents. read_page (topic naming the document) the document(s) listing positions "
            "with quantities, units, requirement references (bill of quantities / position overview). Documents locked "
            "-> register interest first. One read per document. Then done, listing what you saved.")


@register
class TenderScraper(SiteScraper):
    role = "tender"
    browser = 0
    max_steps = 28
    hints = ("Portal habits: cookie wall after login; error pages that go away on retry; survey popups and decoy "
             "'open'/'accept' links leading away (close popups with their x button); documents may need expression of "
             "interest first, may open in viewers/iframes or ZIP downloads (prefer viewer); Q&A list paged, answers in "
             "collapsed rows inside iframes; dates may be in other timezone.")

    def goal(self) -> str:
        return ("Collect tender data for the reference in context. Do NOT enter or submit a bid.\n"
                "1. Log in, accept necessary cookies, open the tender (search its reference if not listed).\n"
                "2. read_page tender overview with topic 'tender overview' (reference, buyer, deadline + timezone).\n"
                "3. Documents locked -> register interest now.\n"
                "4. Then done (other agents read Q&A and documents).")

    def required(self):
        return [(("q&a", "bieterfrage", "frage", "question"), QA_JOB),
                (("leistungsverzeichnis", "positions", "quantities", "bill"),
                 "Open this tender's documents and read_page the bill of quantities / position overview with topic "
                 "'bill of quantities'. Then done.")]

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            first = await self.browse_until_done(self.goal(), max_steps=14)
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", first["summary"])
            # main tab: documents; new tab: Q&A (shares the login)
            await asyncio.gather(self.browse_until_done(DOCS_JOB, attempts=2, max_steps=20),
                                 self.browse_in_tabs([QA_JOB], max_steps=20))
            for keywords, job in self.required():
                if self.ctx.time_left() > 90 and not any(k in self.saved_topics() for k in keywords):
                    self.log.warning("nothing saved for %s: focused browse", keywords)
                    await self.browse(job, max_steps=15)
        finally:
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"done.{self.role}", True)

---
name: swarm-run-findings
description: What test runs on 2026-10-10 showed about where the swarm loses data (ERP, matcher, mail duplication, logs)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Test runs on 2026-10-10 (run_d1ee, run_e058, run_9643) all scored quality 10: decision and reference were right, and every position was omitted.

- **ERP item browses run out of 30 steps.** Each one spends its steps on login checks, the maintenance dialog, "Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar", MM03 and the F4 search. A record opens only by clicking its row in the F4 list; direct /material/<no> URLs return 404. Prices and stock are almost never read.
- **The matcher drops candidates that were collected.** The F4 list has no certification, so an empty value counts as a mismatch. A requirement given as usable stroke needs the mail's reserve value, and without it nothing matches. With zero materials, BidCalculator returned no_bid (run_9643).
- **Collection ends too early.** The swarm leaves COLLECT about 8–10 min in, with lots of time left, because the agent's "done" counts as success even when its summary says data is missing.
- **Mail tabs read the same messages.** Each tab searches "<ref> <topic>", logs in again and passes the slider gate again.
- **The platform log keeps only the last ~2–3 min.** The verbose browser_use output (pydantic validation dumps) pushes out the analyst lines.
- **Flash-mode validation error.** The model puts two actions in one object, e.g. {"record":…, "click":…}.

**Why:** these points decide quality now; speed is already good (collection takes 8–10 min).
**How to apply:** fix the ERP flow (search-list stage, then per-material stage), make the matcher tolerate unknown fields, add gap-driven follow-up browses, dedupe mail reads, and reduce log noise. See [[atira-cli-path]].

Speed is now fine: collection takes 8–10 min. The problem is quality. The last three test runs all scored **10/100**: tender reference and decision were right, and **every position was omitted**. The tab-isolation fix worked: all 5 ERP catalogue groups returned results in `run_9643`, and agents no longer type over each other. But the matcher still accepted no materials, and that run is now submitting **no_bid**.

You're right that a lot of browsing is repeated, but the bigger loss is that data we do collect is thrown away or never finished.

## Pain points

**1. ERP workers repeat the same setup and run out of steps before the useful part.**
- Each of the 5 ERP item jobs repeats the same path: login check, maintenance dialog, MM03, F4 search help, search. That costs about 10–15 of its 30 steps.
- The maintenance dialog and "Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar" come back on every page load, in every tab.
- A material record opens only by clicking its row in the F4 list; direct `/material/<no>` URLs return 404.
- Agents also open candidates that the result list already shows don't fit (for example a different pressure).
- So status, prices and stock were almost never read. Agent summaries say it directly: "could NOT be opened because the step budget was exhausted…"

**2. The matcher throws away candidates we did find.**
- The F4 list shows bore, stroke, pressure and mounting, but not certification. A missing certification counts as a mismatch, so those candidates are dropped ("no exact match among the ERP records read").
- When a requirement is given as usable stroke, the matcher needs the reserve value from the technical-release mail. If that mail wasn't read, no candidate can match.
- With zero materials, `BidCalculator` sets `decision: no_bid`. That loses even the 5 decision points; a signed partial bid would keep them.

**3. Collection ends too early.**
- `browse_until_done` treats the agent's `done` as success even when its own summary says "prices/stock NOT verified".
- The swarm moved on to VERIFY at 7:44 and 9:45 with over 6,600 s of the 2-hour test-run budget left. In a 20-min scored run that would still leave about 10 min unused.
- Nothing turns the verifier's list of missing data into new browsing.

**4. Mail agents read the same messages several times.**
- Each mail tab searches `<reference> <topic>`. Most mails name the reference, so the result lists overlap and several tabs open the same messages.
- In an earlier run the discount mails were read by two browses (the analyst reported 2/2, then 3/4 valid messages).
- Every tab also logs in again and passes the slider gate again, because the login does not carry over to new tabs.

**5. Earlier ERP split (now removed).** `ErpHelper`, `ErpHelperTender` and `ErpScraper` searched the same catalogue groups (GR-6333 and GR-6617 were each searched twice). The shared queue removed that duplication, but not the repeated setup from point 1.

**6. We lose the logs that would show these problems.** The platform log for a run keeps only roughly the last 2–3 minutes of lines. browser_use's per-step output, including 50-line validation dumps, pushes out the early lines. For `run_9643` nothing before 07:37 survives, so the brief, tender, spec and mail analyst results can't be checked afterwards.

**7. Flash-mode reply format errors.** The "37–53 validation errors" happen because the model packs two actions into one object, e.g. `{"record":…, "click":…}`. Each one costs a retry call.

## Proposed solutions, in order of impact

1. **Split ERP work into two stages.**
   - Stage A, one browse per catalogue group: search and `read_page` the result list only, about 8 steps.
   - Then code compares the list rows with the requirement (bore, pressure, mounting, stroke). The rules allow this, since it filters a result set the model chose.
   - Stage B, one job per matching material, run in parallel tabs: click the row, then read all tabs, VK13 prices and MMBE stock in one `read_page(urls=[...])`.
   - No step is spent on candidates that don't fit, and each job is short enough to finish.
2. **Share what one agent learns about a site.**
   - Once one agent finds the working path (for example that records open from the F4 row, or which transaction URL works), it posts it to the blackboard.
   - Later jobs on that site get it as a hint instead of finding it out again.
   - Login and gate state stay in the main tab, so worker tabs start at the search screen.
3. **Make the matcher tolerate missing values.**
   - A missing field (certification not shown, reserve not read) should count as "unknown", not "mismatch".
   - The best candidate with unknowns becomes a provisional material and triggers a targeted follow-up read.
   - Never return `no_bid` just because materials are missing: submit a signed bid with the missing positions omitted instead.
4. **Fill gaps with targeted follow-up browses.**
   - After COLLECT, the verifier lists exactly what is missing ("price for HZ-x", "stock for HZ-y", "reserve mail for rev R").
   - Each gap becomes a short job in its own tab while the time left is above a limit (e.g. 4 min in a scored run).
   - This uses the 8–10 min currently left unused.
5. **Read each mail once.**
   - One tab searches the reference alone, in inbox and archive, and the model chooses the relevant messages from that list.
   - Those message URLs are read in one `read_page(urls=[...])`, split across tabs only if there are many.
   - `read_page` skips any URL already saved on the blackboard, for every agent and site.
6. **Cut log noise.**
   - Set browser_use's logger to WARNING and drop the pydantic dumps.
   - Log one line per step plus each analyst result.
   - Print a compact board summary at the end, so the platform log keeps the evidence.
7. **Fix the flash reply format.** Add one example to `FLASH_SYSTEM` showing that each action is its own list item: `"action":[{"click":{...}},{"record":{...}}]`.

All of this is still an outline; no code has changed. Points 1, 3 and 4 decide quality and should come first.

The last log query for `run_9643` came back and adds three findings to the outline:

- **The matcher marked a released material as blocked.**
  - The ERP agent read HZ-1609 as "Materialstatus 01 = FREIGEGEBEN", with all five technical attributes matching requirement A-1.
  - The matcher still reported 01.01 as "only blocked matches".
  - In `merge_materials` (`agents/analyze_materials.py:73`), any page that extracts `is_active: false` overrides a `true` from another page, and nothing can set it back.
  - So one wrong reading, probably from a search-list or legend page, outvotes the record's own status tab.
  - Fix: trust the status from the material's own record page over list pages, and treat conflicting readings as "unknown", not "blocked".
- **One agent found a shortcut the others didn't get.** It reports "Search for GR-6617 succeeded via URL", meaning it reached the F4 result list by URL instead of through the dialogs. The other four workers kept clicking through. This is exactly what solution 2 (sharing what agents learn about a site) is for.
- **Price scales are a second click deeper.** The condition record was read (valid 2027, USD, FX key, price unit 100, en-US format), but the quantity scales sit behind "Mengenstaffeln öffnen" and the step budget ran out first. The per-material job in solution 1 should open that register explicitly.

So in this run the ERP side had enough to price at least 01.01, and our own merge code threw it away. That moves the matcher fix (solution 3) to the top, next to the ERP split.

"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.

Time: non-SUBMIT phases are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0), then SUBMIT always runs.
Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import logging
import os
import pkgutil
from pathlib import Path

import agents as agents_pkg
from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S, Context
from swarm.llm import LLM

log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")


def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):
        importlib.import_module(f"agents.{mod.name}")
    return list(REGISTRY)


def select(classes: list[type[Agent]], only: str | None) -> list[type[Agent]]:
    if not only:
        return classes
    wanted = {n.strip() for n in only.split(",") if n.strip()}
    return [c for c in classes if (c.name or c.__name__) in wanted or c.__name__ in wanted]


async def _run_agent(agent: Agent, deadline_bound: bool) -> None:
    try:
        budget = agent.ctx.time_left() if deadline_bound else agent.ctx.seconds_left() - FINAL_MARGIN_S
        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=max(1.0, budget))
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, "timed out")
        log.warning("%s timed out", agent.name)
    except Exception as error:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        log.exception("%s failed", agent.name)


async def run_swarm(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool, env=os.environ):
    board = Blackboard()
    preload = env.get("SWARM_BOARD_IN")
    if preload and not scored:                       # never replay data in a scored run
        board = Blackboard.load(Path(preload))
    ctx = Context(task=task, board=board, llm=LLM(), pool=BrowserPool(playwright), scored=scored)
    classes = select(discover(), env.get("SWARM_ONLY"))
    log.info("agents: %s", [c.__name__ for c in classes])
    for phase in Phase:
        agents = [c(ctx) for c in classes if c.phase == phase]
        if not agents:
            continue
        bound = phase != Phase.SUBMIT
        if bound and ctx.time_left() <= 0:
            log.warning("skipping phase %s: out of time", phase.name)
            continue
        log.info("phase %s: %s (%.0fs left)", phase.name, [a.name for a in agents], ctx.seconds_left())
        await asyncio.gather(*(_run_agent(a, bound) for a in agents))
        if not scored:
            board.dump(BOARD_DUMP)
    log.info("model calls: %d tokens: %s errors: %d", ctx.llm.calls, ctx.llm.tokens, len(board.errors))
    if (task.get("submission") or {}).get("kind", "api") != "api":
        log.info("answer (entered on the website): %s", board.get("answer"))
        return None                      # a "site" submission was entered by the submitter agent
    return board.get("answer")
"""Agent base class and registry. One agent = one file in `agents/`, registered with @register."""
import enum
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class Phase(enum.IntEnum):
    COLLECT = 1   # scrapers: read the sites, post Evidence
    ANALYZE = 2   # analyzers: turn evidence into structured facts (quantities, requirements, candidate materials...)
    VERIFY = 3    # verifiers: cross-check authority / dates / tender reference / superseded records
    COMPUTE = 4   # calculators: deterministic arithmetic, set results["bid"]
    SUBMIT = 5    # fills the configurator, signs; ALWAYS runs, with reserved time


REGISTRY: list[type["Agent"]] = []


def register(cls):
    REGISTRY.append(cls)
    return cls


class Agent(ABC):
    name: str = ""               # defaults to the class name
    phase: Phase = Phase.COLLECT
    browser: int | None = None   # index of the browser this agent drives (0-3), None = no browser

    def __init__(self, ctx):
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.name = self.name or type(self).__name__
        self.log = logging.getLogger(self.name)

    @abstractmethod
    async def run(self) -> None:
        """Read from `self.ctx.board`, do the work, write Evidence / results back. Raise on failure (it is logged;
        other agents carry on). Stop early when `self.ctx.time_left() <= 0`."""
"""Everything an agent gets: the task, the blackboard, the model, the browsers and the clock."""
import asyncio
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import run as contract
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.llm import LLM

# Collecting and analysing stop this long before expiry; the rest belongs to SUBMIT (filling the bid form and signing
# takes several minutes of browser steps). SUBMIT itself stops FINAL_MARGIN_S before expiry.
SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 540))
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40


@dataclass
class Context:
    task: dict
    board: Blackboard
    llm: LLM
    pool: object                      # swarm.browser_pool.BrowserPool (None in unit tests)
    scored: bool = False              # True in a real run (has a run token); False for local scouting
    t0: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    _locks: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)
    shared: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False)   # in-memory objects agents share (queues); never dumped

    @property
    def brief(self) -> str:
        return self.task["brief"]

    def site(self, site_id: str) -> dict:
        """The access entry (siteId, url, credentials) of a website, e.g. ctx.site("erp")."""
        for entry in self.task["access"]:

"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.

Time: non-SUBMIT phases are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0), then SUBMIT always runs.
Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import logging
import os
import pkgutil
from pathlib import Path

import agents as agents_pkg
from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S, Context
from swarm.llm import LLM

log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")


def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):
        importlib.import_module(f"agents.{mod.name}")
    return list(REGISTRY)


def select(classes: list[type[Agent]], only: str | None) -> list[type[Agent]]:
    if not only:
        return classes
    wanted = {n.strip() for n in only.split(",") if n.strip()}
    return [c for c in classes if (c.name or c.__name__) in wanted or c.__name__ in wanted]


async def _run_agent(agent: Agent, deadline_bound: bool) -> None:
    try:
        budget = agent.ctx.time_left() if deadline_bound else agent.ctx.seconds_left() - FINAL_MARGIN_S
        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=max(1.0, budget))
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, "timed out")
        log.warning("%s timed out", agent.name)
    except Exception as error:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        log.exception("%s failed", agent.name)


async def run_swarm(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool, env=os.environ):
    board = Blackboard()
    preload = env.get("SWARM_BOARD_IN")
    if preload and not scored:                       # never replay data in a scored run
        board = Blackboard.load(Path(preload))
    ctx = Context(task=task, board=board, llm=LLM(), pool=BrowserPool(playwright), scored=scored)
    classes = select(discover(), env.get("SWARM_ONLY"))
    log.info("agents: %s", [c.__name__ for c in classes])
    for phase in Phase:
        agents = [c(ctx) for c in classes if c.phase == phase]
        if not agents:
            continue
        bound = phase != Phase.SUBMIT
        if bound and ctx.time_left() <= 0:
            log.warning("skipping phase %s: out of time", phase.name)
            continue
        log.info("phase %s: %s (%.0fs left)", phase.name, [a.name for a in agents], ctx.seconds_left())
        await asyncio.gather(*(_run_agent(a, bound) for a in agents))
        if not scored:
            board.dump(BOARD_DUMP)
    log.info("model calls: %d tokens: %s errors: %d", ctx.llm.calls, ctx.llm.tokens, len(board.errors))
    if (task.get("submission") or {}).get("kind", "api") != "api":
        log.info("answer (entered on the website): %s", board.get("answer"))
        return None                      # a "site" submission was entered by the submitter agent
    return board.get("answer")
"""Agent base class and registry. One agent = one file in `agents/`, registered with @register."""
import enum
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class Phase(enum.IntEnum):
    COLLECT = 1   # scrapers: read the sites, post Evidence
    ANALYZE = 2   # analyzers: turn evidence into structured facts (quantities, requirements, candidate materials...)
    VERIFY = 3    # verifiers: cross-check authority / dates / tender reference / superseded records
    COMPUTE = 4   # calculators: deterministic arithmetic, set results["bid"]
    SUBMIT = 5    # fills the configurator, signs; ALWAYS runs, with reserved time


REGISTRY: list[type["Agent"]] = []


def register(cls):
    REGISTRY.append(cls)
    return cls


class Agent(ABC):
    name: str = ""               # defaults to the class name
    phase: Phase = Phase.COLLECT
    browser: int | None = None   # index of the browser this agent drives (0-3), None = no browser

    def __init__(self, ctx):
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.name = self.name or type(self).__name__
        self.log = logging.getLogger(self.name)

    @abstractmethod
    async def run(self) -> None:
        """Read from `self.ctx.board`, do the work, write Evidence / results back. Raise on failure (it is logged;
        other agents carry on). Stop early when `self.ctx.time_left() <= 0`."""

280	    info = event.get("targetInfo") or {}
281	    if info.get("openerId"):
282	        _OPENERS[info["targetId"]] = info["openerId"]
283	    await _handle_target_attached(self, event)

291	async def _enable_page_monitoring_routed(self, cdp_session) -> None:
292	    """browser-use registers one lifecycle handler per page target, but the CDP client keeps only ONE handler per event
293	    (the last one), and that handler drops events of every other target. With several tabs in a browser, navigations
294	    in all but the last-attached tab then waited for load events that never came (3-8 s per navigation). Here one
295	    handler per client routes each event to the queue of its own target."""
296	    await _enable_page_monitoring(self, cdp_session)
297	    events = getattr(cdp_session, "_lifecycle_events", None)
298	    if events is None:
299	        return
300	    routes = self.__dict__.setdefault("_lifecycle_routes", {})
301	    routes[cdp_session.target_id] = events
302	
303	    def route(event, session_id=None):
304	        target = self.get_target_id_from_session_id(session_id) if session_id else None
305	        queue = routes.get(target)
306	        if queue is not None:
307	            queue.append({"name": event.get("name", "unknown"), "loaderId": event.get("loaderId", "none"),
308	                          "timestamp": asyncio.get_event_loop().time()})
309	
310	    cdp_session.cdp_client.register.Page.lifecycleEvent(route)
311
